The current best estimate for the age of the universe is approximately 13.8 billion years.

This estimate comes from measurements of the cosmic microwave background radiation, the oldest light in the universe, as well as observations of the oldest stars and other cosmological data. The age of the universe is calculated by tracing back the expansion of the universe to the initial hot, dense state known as the Big Bang.

Some key facts about the age of the universe:

- The universe began with the Big Bang around 13.8 billion years ago.
- After the Big Bang, the universe expanded and cooled over billions of years to its present state.
- The cosmic microwave background radiation, emitted just 380,000 years after the Big Bang, provides a key piece of evidence for the Big Bang model.
- Measurements of the abundances of light elements like hydrogen, helium, and lithium also support the Big Bang theory and the age of the universe.
- Observations of the oldest stars in our galaxy provide an independent estimate for the minimum age of the universe, which is also around 13.8 billion years.

So in summary, the best current scientific estimate, based on multiple lines of evidence, puts the age of the universe at approximately 13.8 billion years old.
